residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been a resident of Arkansas for at least 60 days before filing and for 3 months before the final decree is entered.

waitingPeriod.description: No final decree of divorce shall be granted until at least 30 days after the date the complaint is filed. Ark. Code §9-12-307(b).

noFault.name: 18-Month Separation
noFault.description: The parties have lived separate and apart for eighteen (18) consecutive months without cohabitation

fault.name: Impotency
fault.description: Impotency at the time of marriage

fault.name: Felony or Infamous Crime
fault.description: Conviction of a felony or other infamous crime

fault.name: Cruel and Barbarous Treatment
fault.description: Cruel and barbarous treatment endangering the life of the other party

fault.name: Personal Indignities
fault.description: Personal indignities rendering the other party's condition intolerable

fault.name: Incurable Insanity
fault.description: Incurable insanity of either party for at least three years

groundsForDissolution.notes: Arkansas has both fault and no-fault grounds. The no-fault ground requires 18 months of continuous separation. Fault grounds are frequently used when the waiting period is not met.

propertyDivision.description: Arkansas uses equitable distribution. Marital property is divided equitably. The court considers the length of the marriage, age and health of the parties, occupation, amount and sources of income, vocational skills, employability, and the contribution of each party to the acquisition of property.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Arkansas distinguishes between marital and non-marital property. Non-marital property includes property acquired before the marriage, by gift, or by inheritance, and remains with the owning spouse unless commingled.

filingFees.notes: Arkansas filing fees are approximately $165 for a complaint for divorce but may vary by county. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via an In Forma Pauperis motion.

basic.name: Affidavit of Financial Means
basic.description: Disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order granting the divorce

service.name: Summons
service.description: Service on defendant via sheriff or process server

service.name: Waiver and Acceptance of Service
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Child Support Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Ark. Admin. Order No. 10 (income shares model)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Arkansas Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file a response within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Arkansas must file a response within 30 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Arkansas uses an income shares model per Administrative Order No. 10. Both parents' net incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Arkansas Family Support Chart based on combined income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust. Credits for overnight visitation may apply.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Arkansas allows alimony based on the need of one spouse and the ability of the other to pay. The court considers the financial circumstances, earning capacity, length of the marriage, and other relevant factors. Alimony may be temporary, rehabilitative, or permanent.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: There is no formula; the court has broad discretion. Alimony is generally not awarded in short marriages without significant disparity.

court.name: Circuit Court, Domestic Relations Division
court.description: Divorce cases are filed in the Circuit Court, Domestic Relations Division, in the county where the plaintiff resides.
